To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in the obese patient with bronchial obstructive disease, the functional characteristics of hypoventilation are not significantly modified by different postures, and that the ratio between TLC measured in squatting position to that in standing position x 100 can be considered a useful indicator of the diaphragmatic function in the evaluation of the respiratory functional condition of the patient.
in obese patients with hypoventilation the diaphragm is not able to adapt to postural changes.

the respiratory mechanics are different in obese patients and normal weight individuals, that in obese patients there is no diaphragmatic adjustment in different postures, that the diaphragm of obese patients is not active and the diaphragmatic passivity index can be used to assess the diaphragmatic function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the respiratory function in obese subjects and in particular the influence of posture on respiratory mechanics.
the evaluation of respiratory function in obese patients with hypoventilation.

the evaluation of the influence of posture on the respiratory function tests in patients with obesity hypoventilation syndrome and the development of a method for evaluating the functional condition of diaphragm.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a) the respiratory function tests in obese patients should be performed in standing position and in squatting; b) the plethysmosgraphic method is the best one to use in these cases; c) the diaphragmatic passivity index is a useful parameter in assessing the diaphragmatic function in obese patients.
the functional assessment of obese patients should be carried out in the squatting position.
the functional evaluation of obese patients with hypoventilation should be carried out with a plethysmograph in standing posture.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the respiratory function examination in the obese patient with hypoventilation is best performed with the patient standing and that the use of the plethysymographic method is preferable to the helium dilution method.
the diaphragm is the main respiratory muscle involved in the respiratory disorders of obesity.
the functional assessment of respiratory disorders in the obese should not be based on single measurements but on the evaluation of the respiratory mechanics in different postures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the diaphragm in patients with hypoventilation is not able to adapt to the changes of posture and that this is due to the lack of the phrenophrenical reflex and to the muscle flattening.
the diaphragm of patients with alveolar hypo-ventilation and bronchial obstruction is not able to adjust itself to changes in posture.
the functional evaluation of obese patients must include respiratory function tests carried out in different postures, in order to assess the functional condition of diaphragm.
